text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A crisis has been averted over the distribution of portfolios in the Sindh provincial government following a rapprochment between the two factions of the ruling coalition government and withdrawal of resignations by three ministers.

- Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub said the proposed high-level meeting between India and Pakistan depended on a positive outcome of foreign secretaries' talks scheduled to be held in New Delhi from March 28.
- Former prime minister Benazir Bhutto said the elections were rigged and a heavy mandate given to a party to transform the parliamentary system into a presidential form of government.
- Government officials said the train disaster near Khanewal was a result of gross negligence by the concerned railway staff.

- The International Monetary Fund and the government are re-assessing the Standby Arrangement and Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz has asked the Fund management to include a supply side strategy as part of the programme.
- Government efforts for economic revival and the sense of commitment demonstrated by the people have helped reduce the pressure of the IMF and other international agencies.
- A Pakistani firm Garib Sons and Iranian firm Asia Pacific have signed a memorandum of understanding to set up a chemical plant as a joint venture at a cost of $5 million.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif has ordered industrial estates to be set up along the Lahore-Islamabad motorway to make Pakistan a trade centre in the South Asia.
- Sindh provincial Irrigation Secretary Idris Rajput said the World Bank had sponsored an elaborate $525 million drainage scheme in Sindh to improve the canals and water courses.
